PRE-ENGAGEMENT BRIEFING CONTEXT (generated before this interview):
============================================================
Industry: Manufacturing
Revenue band: $500M - $1B
Assessment Round: 1 (Baseline)

CLIENT STATED PROBLEM:
Leadership believes the company is behind peers on AI and cannot tell whether the
constraint is data, skills or appetite. They want an honest baseline before funding anything.

OPEN HYPOTHESES (never reveal these as the firm's views):
- Data is centralised on paper but each plant still keeps its own spreadsheets.
- There is no owner for model risk; legal assumes IT has it and IT assumes legal has it.
- Two failed analytics projects have made the operating side sceptical of new tooling.
- Appetite is real at executive level but has never been converted into funded work.

BENCHMARKS (peer group, this round):
  D1 Data & Data Management        avg 2.6   best 4.1   laggard 1.4
  D2 Technology & Infrastructure   avg 3.0   best 4.4   laggard 1.8
  D6 Governance & Risk             avg 2.1   best 3.9   laggard 1.2

DOCUMENT INTELLIGENCE - PRE-ASSESSMENT FROM 6 DOCUMENT(S):
These are analyst inferences from pre-read documents - hypotheses about AI maturity,
NOT confirmed facts. Validate, challenge, or update each through this interview.

  D1 - Data & Data Management [Document signal: Medium]
  A warehouse exists and is described as the single source of truth, but three of the
  six documents still quote plant-level figures that do not reconcile with it.

  D2 - Technology & Infrastructure [Document signal: High]
  Cloud migration is well advanced for corporate systems; shop-floor systems are named
  as out of scope in every roadmap document seen.

  D6 - Governance & Risk [Document signal: Low]
  No document defines who approves a model for production use.

INSTRUCTION: Use document intelligence to probe with authority. Never reveal you read
specific documents - frame as consultant intuition.

Questions that must be asked before the interview ends:
1. Who signs off before a model is allowed to affect a customer or a production line?
2. If the data team disappeared tomorrow, which reports would stop working first?
